heading: What the user accepts
text:
### What the user accepts [LNLS.1.2]

`linear_scan: false` is an advanced, opt-in constraint.  Users who choose it
accept:

- No `json`-typed slots.
- No interpolated string producing run-time-novel strings.
- No regex match without a declared slot width bound.
- No cross-pattern comparison that lacks an equality anchor.
- No sketch-backed series aggregations (quantile, count_distinct with
  tolerance, HLL via tolerance, entropy) — the sketch / accuracy forms are
  already removed for everyone ([LNLS.3.5]), so `linear_scan: false` adds no
  restriction here.
- No series membership / frequency read (`contains`, `count_of`) without a
  `capacity` ([LSER.13.14]) or the `sample <n>` reservoir — see [LNLS.3.11].
- No string ordering (`<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` on String-typed values in
  cross-pattern position).

In return they get the algorithmic properties in [LNLS.5] and the
simplified T_wcet formula in [LNLS.7].
